from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

@dataclass
class Num:   value: float
@dataclass
class Var:   name: str
@dataclass
class BinOp: op: str; left: Any; right: Any

def show(node):
    match node:
        case Num(value=v):                return str(int(v) if v == int(v) else v)
        case Var(name=n):                 return n
        case BinOp(op=o, left=l, right=r): return f"({show(l)} {o} {show(r)})"

def size(node):
    match node:
        case BinOp(left=l, right=r): return 1 + size(l) + size(r)
        case _:                      return 1

OPS = {"+": lambda a, b: a + b, "-": lambda a, b: a - b,
       "*": lambda a, b: a * b, "/": lambda a, b: a / b}

def fold(node):
    """Rewrite the tree, returning a NEW tree with constant subtrees collapsed."""
    match node:
        case BinOp(op=o, left=l, right=r):
            l, r = fold(l), fold(r)              # children first: bottom-up
            if isinstance(l, Num) and isinstance(r, Num):
                if o == "/" and r.value == 0:
                    return BinOp(o, l, r)        # refuse: leave the error for runtime
                return Num(OPS[o](l.value, r.value))
            return BinOp(o, l, r)
        case _:
            return node

examples = [
    BinOp("+", BinOp("*", Num(2), Num(3)),
               BinOp("*", Var("x"), BinOp("+", Num(4), Num(1)))),
    BinOp("*", BinOp("+", Num(1), Num(2)), BinOp("-", Num(10), Num(4))),
    BinOp("+", Var("y"), Var("z")),
    BinOp("/", Num(1), Num(0)),
]

print(f"  {'before':34} {'after':22} {'nodes':>12}")
for tree in examples:
    folded = fold(tree)
    before, after = size(tree), size(folded)
    pct = 100 * (before - after) / before
    print(f"  {show(tree):34} {show(folded):22} {before:2} -> {after:2}  ({pct:4.0f}% gone)")

print("\n=== Does folding need a second pass? ===")
deep = BinOp("+", Num(1), BinOp("+", Num(2), BinOp("+", Num(3), Num(4))))
print(f"  {show(deep)}")
once = fold(deep)
print(f"  after one pass:  {show(once)}  (nodes {size(deep)} -> {size(once)})")
twice = fold(once)
print(f"  after two passes: {show(twice)}")
print("  Because fold() recurses into the children BEFORE testing the parent,")
print("  one bottom-up pass already reaches a fixed point here.")
description: A fold function rewrites an AST bottom-up: it recursively folds children first, then if both children are Num nodes, computes the operation and returns a new Num node. Includes division-by-zero guard and demonstrates single-pass fixed point.

steps.description: Dataclass AST nodes: Num holds float value, Var holds name string, BinOp has op, left, right. These are the tree types the optimizer transforms.
show function uses match/case to pretty-print: Num prints value (int if whole), Var prints name, BinOp prints infix with parentheses.
size function counts nodes: BinOp counts 1 plus sizes of children; other nodes count as 1.
OPS dictionary maps operator strings to lambda functions for the four arithmetic operations.

fold matches BinOp and recursively folds left and right children first (bottom-up). If both are Num and the operator is not division by zero, return Num of the computed result. Otherwise rebuild BinOp with folded children. Non-BinOp nodes return unchanged.
Bottom-up order: children folded before parent tested. Division guard at lines 31-32 refuses to fold 1/0 to avoid turning runtime error into compile-time error.

Output shows node counts: 9->5 (44% gone), 7->1 (86% gone), 3->3 (0%), 3->3 (0%).
Deep nested addition (1+(2+(3+4))) folds to 10 in one pass (7->1 nodes); second pass shows no change, proving single bottom-up pass reaches fixed point.
